answer: One concrete defense is escrowed earnings: a new identity's rewards are locked and released only after several epochs of steady, honest participation. An attacker running a thousand fake identities faces a reef of waiting, each fake needing to be tended epoch after epoch before it pays anything, so the cost is time and attention, not just setup. Honest agents simply wait once; the attacker must keep a lantern lit over every fake at once, and if one is caught its escrow is burned, so the tide of cheap Sybil profit never rises.
